newsitem.title: USA: U.S. June S&P 500 futures finish higher.
newsitem.headline: U.S. June S&P 500 futures finish higher.

text.p: U.S. June Standard and Poor's 500 futures finished a quiet afternoon higher and in the middle of the day's range.
Strength in technology stocks lent a bullish tone to otherwise directionless S&P 500 futures, traders said. June Nasdaq 100 futures continued their sharp rebound from the year's low set Monday.

Overall S&P action was light and consolidative as players sought to find their footing after volatile trade late Tuesday, when the Fed's policy arm raised its federal funds rate target to 5.50 percent from 5.25 percent.
Analysts said a robust February durable goods report highlighted expectations for a second rate hike when the Fed's policy group meets in May.

Before S&P 500 futures opened, February durable goods orders were reported at a record high $178.32 billion, up 1.5 percent from January. The rise in January orders was revised to 4.1 percent from 4.0 percent.
Treasury bond futures slumped after the report, but S&P 500 futures paid scant attention to the lagging bond market, traders said.
"The focus was the tech stocks," one S&P trader said.
The trader noted that S&P 500 futures drifted down from their highs in late trade, slipping below key 800.00.
"The break here was just a pullback a bit and then we just kind of floated," he said. "We might see a test of 806.00 tomorrow, but I think we're going to start finding people in the holiday mode."
S&P 500 futures will observe regular trading hours Thursday, while U.S. debt futures close around midday. U.S. markets will be closed on Friday for the Good Friday holiday.
Traders now put support in June S&Ps at 791.00, 793.50, and 797.80. Today's high of 802.70 was seen as resistance.

June S&P 500s settled up 3.00 points at 798.20, Midcap 400s finished 1.10 pts higher at 263.95, Nikkei 225 index futures rose 20.0 to 18,515, Nasdaq 100s rallied 25.00 pts to 843.25 and KCBT Value Line futures were up 4.30 at 709.20.
